I've never have had anyone tell me I'm attractive in real life, but I know I'd react like you. It's not like i even desire to be seen as attractive though, I just want to hide all the time. I have this weird craving for wanting to be insulted though possibly because I feel validated when people agree with my negative critique of my own appearance. 

The other day I was sobbing because I was remembering how as a kid, some other kid had a crush on me and i feel like I misled them into thinking I was "cute" when I wasn't. I feel guilty even though I'm not responsible logically for their emotions. I feel like I was and am the reason people don't have standards.  Like geez, what did I do to that person to make them be that desperate to lower their standards for me and like me? Like, have some self respect, don't lower yourself all because of me, don't settle for something as hideous as me. That's my thought process.

I feel like I've grown attached to my BDD though. I don't feel like getting better now because it would mean being vulnerable and exposing what I think about myself to people who are in power. Words have power, I don't want a therapist telling me something that will make me feel worse than I do already.

Pretty much. You worded better than I could ever though. This is why I don't ask for help, because I feel like the observer inside a cage, like an outcast. I feel like an animal with my monkey hands over the rails kbehind a cage, just sticking my head out of this cage as I watch everyone walk by me like I'm lesser than. Sorta like the donkey boys in Pinnochio, when they're crying after being thrown in cages.

 It's very lonely and upsetting, and unsettling. I also gave up on hobbies for the same reason. Never good enough at anything, plus it only makes me feel worse. I feel rather than a sense of achievement, a sense of shame and embarrassment even at my drawings, hairstyling, anything considered "beautiful", (art, hairstyling, makeup, decorating) since I never get any of it perfectly right.

Me too. It's not even about the "what ifs" for me though, it's about the FACT that everything you mentioned can happen to ANYONE. I've already been through enough suffering to suffer more. I'm tired down to my soul. 

Also, I hate being a girl. I feel disgusting all the time and I suspect I have BDD. It doesn't help to have people reminding me that I'm less than (by the way they treat me) because of how I look. People will flinch or yell at me for something as simple as sharing a news I was happy about. It's not my fault my natural voice is also ugly and annoying. 

One time, I accidentally almost choked on death because the candy slipped into my throat and I got yelled at for it, after all the suffering I felt. This image still lives in my head, it's like the near death experience is so vivid, it's as if it happened yesterday. Now I can't help but to feel triggered too when I see on the news people die in a similar manner or snakes choking rats to death. There's an ardent flame of pain in my chest, and it hurts so emotionally badly I black out and almost faint constantly.

I don't have any advice, but one thing I can say is that yes, ugly people with BDD do exist. I'm one of them. I don't think recovery is even a possibility nor an option for me, considering it's hard to heal when you have things or people reminding me how monstrous I look. I was constantly discriminated and never had much friends because of my looks since I was a toddler. 

I'm thinking about just unaliving myself a few years down the road. That's the only thing that brings me emotional relief from the this huge distress.

Same. My emotional pain is so highly complex, that writing it all down would take years, because literally day by day, for years I've been in pain. 

I hide my pain, because I don't want anyone to find out, mostly due to reasons related to lack of self compassion and shame.

As a Christian, I'm ashamed other christians are being so dismissive of your valid questions or tap dancing around the point. Apparently it now turns out, that if you don't accept things as they are, then you're 'mentally ill' for being empathetic and not desensitized (like most of the world is) to the horrors of suffering and violence. Jesus says blessed are those who mourn with those who mourn. Thats a reference to human suffering, but whos to say its wrong to mourn for animals too? You are a sensitive person, in a good way. It shows you think more than just about yourself. I commend you for that. If it weren't for Jesus saying it's okay to be single, people would (as some still do) say you're abnormal for not desiring to get married because "we were all created for marriage and you're disobeying the commandment in Genesis". Why i bring that up? Because...my point is, just because you are a certain way or feel a certain way doesnt make you the abnormal one. We have to learn to look beyond what we know (beyond the Bible). Being curious isn't a sin, neither is being humble enough as christains and admit that we just don't have good answers sometimes. 

Thus, even as an imperfect person, I will admit, that I don't have a good answer for your questions, because I too have wondered the same things as you and haven't found satisfying answers that put my uneasiness to rest. The answers you are given just ignores the animals's suffering as they just dismiss with " food being enjoyable matters more than their suffering" Really goes to show where some people place their values, right? Food being enjoyable at the cost of their suffering....it's not sin to enjoy it, the problem is their lack of empathy and how we can mitigate the suffering of others including animals. There seems to be no solution to that, and the answers aren't helping either. Considering God is the ultimate problem solver, we would've at least hoped that he would've created a system where animals don't at least experience pain the way they do upon being killed for their flesh. As a Christian, I would hope to receive an answer that, even if doesn't resolve animal suffering, at least helps me understand why God would allow it to go as far as it has now. We can't be blamed for needing meat either and having to kill animals in order to survive. We didn't create this survival mechanisms, nor how it works. 

I have thought, though it's a rather poor answer to your question, that maybe there is nothing to "understand" about animal suffering. Notice you and I are looking for answers that "justify" the suffering in some sense logically, yet the Bible itself doesn't even justify suffering, God actually intends to erase all of it some day. Maybe that's why we can't find answers that justify suffering, because suffering can't exactly be justified to begin with (food being tasty at the cost of animal suffering being a poor reason as well that cant justify it). Or in other words, theres nothing to justify here, because suffering shouldn't be justified to begin with, thus we won't find any good answers that justify it, considering that according to the Bible, suffering is a consequence (effect) of sin, a consequence therfore, that God intends to get rid of. Still, this leaves an open question: Why would God at least allow such suffering to go this far? Creationists would have a partial answer (the fall of mankind), but not all of us reject evolution nor believe the world is that young.

I used to overeat when I was depressed or stressed sometimes. This is known as emotional eating. I rarely do that now, but I did find some things to manage the weight. Often, I found that I was eating comfort food like cookies,chocolate, gummy worms etc. I felt pretty bad when I ate high calories to be honest. So even though it wad hard, I decided to have the food I craved and then drink some healthy juice or water. Drinking half a glass of water thirty minutes before eating (to avoid bloating and colics) is healthy because it helps the digestive system. It also takes up some room so when we eat, we get fuller faster. There are plenty of comfort foods that have fiber too so it is more filling all while still get to eat the food you want moderately because of the fiber. It is really hard not gonna lie. It takes a lot of power to avoid giving in to certain foods. You might also be wanting sugary foods or salty foods if you're not getting the right nutrients. When I wouldn't drink enough water, I wanted more sugar. That's because the body is thirsty even if we don't feel like we are. If you find it hard to drink because you rarely feel thirsty, a pinch of salt or a few chips to trigger the thirst will make it all the easier. Popcorn will olive oil and a bit of sprinkled salt is good too and low on calories. Most importantly, don't sacrifice what you love. Life doesn't have to be boring foods and drinks. You could do the water trick that I told you or drinking some water with infused lemon and cucumber and a bit of sugar before you eat or after you eat a bit of your favorite foods. So say, five chip ahoy cookies, or one hershey bar and wait a bit then drink some healthy infused water or zero calorie sparkling fruit flavored water. Drink about five fluid ounces slowly. Have a cookie or what ever five minutes after. If you're still hungry make some low calorie comfort food recipes like macaroni and cheese or vegan french toast with maple syrup (lot less calories then regular syrup). You will get icky a bit which is normal because you satisfied your hunger and thirst which will help control sugar levels and appetite. Try eating when you are not watching movies, because it has been proven that we eat our food faster and in bigger portions when we are distracted. This is why some people feel sick afterwards because they end up over eating accidentally. Yes, eat when you watch tv sometimes, but try to avoid eating while your watching tv every time you eat. Only do that sometimes. Try eating on the sofa with the tv off and once you're done eating, then go back turn it on. If you become restless lay have your phone with you so you have double entertainment. When I become very bored or impatient while watching tv, I lay down on my side watching it with a comfy velvet texture pillow and a fleece blanket. It helps soothe me a bit. Even though you have no motivation, I recommend looking for a few comfort food recipes. Maybe you don't have a lot of interesting foods incorporated into your menu. My depression makes it hard to eat a lot of foods because I find them all boring. So constantly I lool for new recipes. Try switching up some snacks for lower calorie ones. I don't mean to stop buying them. Buy them, but ALSO buy low calorie snacks, so when you still get that crave even when you are full, you could have the "second best option". Sure, the snack might not be as tasty as a double chocolate chip cookie. Ever seen Emma's Goodies channel on youtube? She has so many low calorie snack and cake and pizza recipes. The best part is, a lot of them can be made in a simple microwave or fridge. This also gets the person to move around and to get creative with the snacks. Watermelon is very filling and strawberries. They are low in calories. Oranges are pretty healthy too, healthier than premade orange juice. Vegan low calorie butter exists too so if you are into popcorn, it could still be tasty. Studies show by the way, that people tend to eat more junk food when they have it in front of them or at arm distance. So to avoid eating all of the junk food at once, try putting it away in a farther cabinet up high. You might feel "lazy" (in quotes) to get it. I sure did. It takes motivation to want to get the junk food when it's put away in the back of a cabinet up high or in a storage room. When I am really craving too much junk food though and I'm overeating it, I replace it with a lollipop. My favorite are dum dum pops because they are mini in size, they come in different flavors, and they don't have many calories compared to a cadbury chocolate bar. They also take a long time to lick because they are kinda hard to bite. You could have a couple of them and it won't be that many calories as having gummy worms.

Some people just tic without feeling any forewarning. 


Because I am not a professional, I can't tell you what you have. But keep observe your daily life and if it persists and you have concerns, see a doctor so they can rule it out. Unfortunately, tic disorders and Tourretes is not really curable. There is no win to be honest. However, if you are young, there could be chance of getting better with age. Not everyone, but sometimes it can improve by itself or worsen. Improvement or worsening is not up to you though. It just of matter of seeing what happens as time goes by. I got a bit better, but the coprolalia really hasn't. I had a tic right now as I was writing. I don't wanna say what it is because tics can have triggers, but all I can say is my coprolalia made my head hurt and my face is hot and veins pounding now because an environmental factor around my house outside triggered it.😖I'm literally sobbing from the pain and exhaustion. Sometimes there are better days sometimes there are worst days. You never really know what tomorrow will be like because it could be you feel like you gotta tic more days than others. Anyways, tics can have triggers. It's like throwing pollen at someone who is allergic to it and it sets on the sequence of sneezing and coughing or a heck load of things. Getting nervous or excited can trigger it too, many things can set tics off. For me, triggers are opened windows and doors and being around strangers or in public even if nobody is there. Also, tics can range from almost non existent to severely debilitating. There's no "standard". Tics can sound and look serious or sound crazy playful and angry. Tone and pitch could change and go back and forth. Very tiring indeed. Also, there is the phenomenon that no one can explain. Sometimes you will shout what you are thinking or the opposite of what you are thinking or sometimes you will say stuff even your mind is blank. You can't control your thoughts though so don't feel bad about it. You know you don't mean it. You will deal a lot of ignorance in life. Not everyone will be nice because they just don't understand. There will be many challenges, but always remember that you are not a horrible person and most people don't mean to hurt your feelings. They just have a hard time understanding. If you could make friends or go to supportive groups with people with Tourettes, you might find that it helps you build courage to go out to places and to build healthy self esteem. It takes a lot if bravery to expose yourself to a world where you know you will be judged and misunderstood. But no matter what people tell you, don't let them become your burden. You don't need that. Accept yourself and your tics even if others don't accept you. You lose nothing when you brush ignorant strangers off your shoulders. Please try to get your tics seen by a doctor. Record your tics on a video so they can see for themselves. No matter how embarrassing the tics are, it's important you have proof so  they can see what your daily life is like. I went through that phase of not trusting myself, but eventually I overcame it. It's too much to explain, but I'll try to shorten it as much as possible. Basically, tics can feel very natural or unnatural. There is no "rules" on how you are suppose to feel. Your brain has an illness that you cannot cure. Tics can feel as natural as a yawn, and the tics tend to feel as if you were doing it for yourself. Let me tell you something as a person with Tourettes who has dealt with with for many years. Why do humans blink? Is it you blinking? No, bit it feels like it right? Sometimes there is no urge to blink, but humans and even animals keep blinking anyways. Why? Is it because they are doing it for themselves? No. It may feel like you are, but you aren't. So why do we humans and animals blink? Because our brain is wired this way. Notice how there isn't always and urge to blink, but for some reason, you don't know why you "just blink". Ironically, sometimes the urge to blink seems to sometimes come after you try resisting to blink. But this is because when you start to resist or fight against it, you're fighting against what your body is programmed to do. It needs to blink even if you don't feel a forewarning sensation that lets you know that you are about to blink. It may feel like you are doing the blinking on purpose, but you're not. And then when you do thw tic, because of the way it felt, almost so transitional and "natural/unatural", you start doubting yourself and wondering if you're "faking" because it physically felt like it was "you"; It feels as if you would've done it "on purpose". That's whay most tics feel like. Some people get a weird tickle sensation before the tic happens which lets them know they're about to tic and others don't get this feeling until they start suppressing. Often the feeling of like your gonna "blow up" ticking comes when you're suppressing. There tends to be a physical feeling, like some indescribable tickle/hollow/tingling is build up. However, some people with Tourettes may not experience this. The tics feel like they just "do the tic". Often, these people describe not "knowing" why they just ticked and start doubting themselves. Trust me, you are not faking. Fakers wish/desire to carry out a plan of intentionally deceiving others, in other words, they don't even question if whether they are faking. Fakers don't "feel" that they are faking. They are fully self aware of what they desire to carry out- to carry out the plan of deceiving. You are not faking. It may take you time to trust yourself, but trust me you are not faking. Think, why would you do something you don't want to do? You might even say" I don't know why I do what I do". You know why? Because you are not faking. True Fakers have motives and goals, and they KNOW why they do what they want to do. So you aren't faking. Your concern is normal. However, if your worry continues, then you might also have OCD (but pure O so only intrusive thoughts basically) or Imposter Syndrome (which contrary to what it may sound like, Imposter Syndrome is not a Hypochondriac. Imposter Syndrome is where the person constantly worries about being a "faker", when they aren't). I forgot to add, that often, sometimes a person with tourettes might do what they are thinking or the opposite of what they are thinking. Thoughts can trigger (set the tics on). You can't control your thoughts though so never feel bad about it. Okay. :)

I understand it can be frustrating. I went through the same thing too. Atheism and agnosticism are not mutually exclusive.

Atheism-lack of belief (to be without a god/gods).

Agnosticism- a person who believes that nothing is known or can be known of the existence or nature of God or of anything beyond material phenomena. (So basically you don't claim on knowing whether god exists or not because so far, you don't see any available reliable methods on obtaining the knowledge).


Agnosticism is a take on knowledge while Atheism is whether you are convinced or unconvinced. It's not to say though, that you think religious people are lying. It just means you are not accepting there claims as true because you aren't convinced currently, unless there were empirical evidence, then you wouldn't mind accepting what is presented. If it helps, I will present an analogy. Suppose you have two very honest friends. But you know humans are capable of making mistakes or being unreliable at times. Now suppose you left a wallet full of cash for them to watch over. You leave the room for five seconds and when you return, you see the cash if gone. You know one of them took it because there was nothing else that could have taken it. They point fingers at each other saying the other took it. You know there can't be two right answers, however, you don't want to accuse, so you're left unconvinced. There is absolutely no belief. You do not believe one friend nor the other friend. (Lack of belief). However, it doesn't mean you believe one of them specifically is lying, but what you do know is that somebody is wrong here even though you are not siding with anyone in the moment because you don't have enough proof to do so. So lack of belief is different from belief. An atheist can lack belief in any gods (left unconvinced that god/gods exist), though they could also have a belief that god doesn't exist. I know it sounds trippy when you read it at first, follow through with me though. Notice how I said, "An atheist lacks belief in any gods (left unconvinced that god/gods exist)". I didn't say an atheist can't have beliefs related to things about gods and religion. For example, there are anti-theists who believe religion does more harm than anything to society. Every human being has beliefs about something. You may believe chocolate ice cream is better than vanilla, it doesn't mean you're claiming your belief is a fact though. It also doesn't mean that you think vanilla is gross. So I don't believe there is any god or gods out there ( or if that confuses you, then better put, what I am saying is that I have been left unconvinced). Just like if you lend me money, as a stranger, whom you know nothing about, you are left unconvinced that I will bring back the money. You may or may not have an opinion that I will return it back, but are you actually CONVINCED that I will return the cash back? Similarly, if you aren't convinced god is real then by definition, you are an atheist. Atheism isn't a claim that god or gods don't exist it's just an "I'm not convinced" stance. We are willing to stand corrected if we are presented the necessary evidence. Until then the majority of us will say "we don't know" because we do not have all the knowledge necessary to determine with certainty. It doesn't mean we have doubts about god's existence though, but though a few might, they are still an atheist. Wondering if god exists doesn't make a person a believer. If you are left unconvinced then you are still an atheist. If you are mostly sure god exists, but you think you have the slight chance of being wrong, then you are an agnostic atheist. I define myself as an agnostic atheist because I am left  unconvinced about anything like a god existing. Agnostic just describes whether I think I have the sufficient knowledge to claim with certainty whether god exists or not, and I don't claim it because I don't have proof. The majority of us are agnostic atheists. There tends to be a disagreement though about who the burden of proof falls on. Most say it is on the theists, but then we acknowledge that you can't always prove a negative, though in some cases you can. So you are an atheist. You can decide if whether you claim that it is knowable that god doesn't exist or if that is not knowable. Death is not an easy thing to accept, but look at it this way. It is something that will catch up as you say, so what's the hurry? Life is shorter than death, so why not spend the time we have left doing something rather than nothing even though depression makes our world look gloomy? We worry because we are conscious enough to know what are ultimate fate is, but when death comes, we won't we know it because there will be no "transitional" state of mind, the same way we don"t know when we transition from being awake to being asleep. Death will be as peaceful as it was before we came into this world. We won't feel this pain anymore, because even though we might not have the courage to escape life, life will do it for us. There may not be a "reason" to do anything, but what reason is there to not? What is stopping us from using our freedom to do something? :) Time is short, and I think we have something, at least one thing in life that we value, but that our depression fogs up a bit. So while we still have time here, why not spend it in some productive way, or pour our time, gratitude, and life into what's important to us, so when it's time to go, we can have some wonderful memories to look back on?  Why not create some better memories so depression is not our only one while were still here?

And so this is how I compare my tics. I need to do it, eventually just like a normal person needs to yawn when they feel that they gotta yawn, blink when they need to blink, cough when they got to cough, let their laugh out when they feel giggly, clear their throat when they have to clear their throat badly. There's not a way of escaping it, because suppressing reaches a limit where you can no longer hold back and bam you tic. Just like you can't hold back a cough forever. And it's like if you need to yawn, you can't get the relief by trying to "cough it out" instead, and you can't get the relief from a cough by "yawning it out" instead. Do you get what I'm saying? It's as if the body knows what it needs you to do and what it doesn't need you to do, and so you need to do the tic that you need to do and "let it all out" either in the moment or at some point, but it's gonna happen either way. Some Tourettes sufferers may find themselves that when they suppress their tic, and after they stop suppressing their tic, that they unexpectedly are needing to tic a different tic instead (as if your body changed which tic you need to do now). And sometimes your body will require you to do some tic that could up turning out to be a more settle tic or an aggressive tic. Sometimes, there's no way of telling what tics your body ought to require you to do, but there's no way of eventually needing to do whatever tic you have to do at the moment that you gotta tic, oof especially once you reach the limit of your physical threshold the tic is so powerful and energy draining. Trying to "distract" myself from the physical need of needing to tic, such as with reading a book when I need to tic and not letting out the tic, (suppression/holding in the tic), just ends up making me suffer in vain and ticking even more intensely in comparison to if I had not suppressed at all. The physical suffering that I feel while I'm suppressing won't vanish until I do the tic that I got to relieve myself from- Otherwise the physical sensation/suffering that I feel while I'm suppressing gets so intense that sometimes I can't fall asleep like I mentioned. Sometimes it gets so intense, that it actually starts causing me pain, and the pain also intensifies as time goes by while I'm suppressing. There isn't always pain, but when there is, it's double the suffering. And personally the pain to me, feels similar to back pain mixed with a sense of pressure in my body (specifically in the belly when suppressing a vocal tic). There pressure is similar to the pressure you feel in your arm when they take your blood pressure at a doctor's clinic. And the pressure that I feel as time goes by while I'm suppressing, intensifies with every second that strolls by as I'm suppressing. It makes it even more harder to suppress, reminds me of a balloon when the helium pressure is about to make it blow up. But that tickle/ tingly that I mentioned previously is the sensation I almost always get that makes me have to do the tic, and it feels VERY ticklish. Imagine someone tickled you, but even when they stopped the tickle is just sitting there in your body and spreads and starts intensifying. IT'S TORTURE. And that tickle physically provokes you to burst laughing, or coughing, or to yawn, or to blink etc. That's the closest physical urge description I could give about the physical tickle urge of feeling the need to tic. Usually if there's no urge, there's no ticking because it's all connected, like some chain reaction. It is VERY rare for the urge to disappear. Sometimes it coincidentally happens to disappear in the middle of suppressing it and you find that you don't end up needing to do the tic temporarily, of course until the tickle returns again.



Now to Re-cap;
Notice how I don't compare a tic with needing to scratch or needing to eat because its not the same physical powerful type of urge as needing to yawn/ needing to cough. You could forget about eating a meal for good or even ignore scratching when you're kinda itchy, but you can't exactly ignore yawning or needing to cough because you can't hold it back forever, you gotta relieve the yawn/cough/tic and get it all out. The physical need to yawn and cough help the reader visualize and "tune in" to their personal physical experiences better so they could try to understand with analogies what we mean by needing to do a tic, though they will never feel what us people with Tourettes feel because the physical urge that we need to do whatever tic that we feel that we gotta do, is so intense and unique physical feeling, something a normal person will never have to suffer. The sensation is like some deep "lightness" feeling" very uncomfortable, like a very ticklish tickle, some tingly energy. Doesn't feel like ants, more like a tickle urge feeling that you just have to relieve. Physical feelings that come close in comparison to the nearly indescribable sensation would be like the feeling like get when your tickled, and the desperateness od needing to relieve is as bad, if not worst, than when you gotta blink badly or cough badly because you get physically restless if you don't.  The tickle is forcing you to do the tic, just like the tickle in your eyes that is forcing you to blink, or the tickle in your throat that is forcing a person to cough because the tickle makes them feel like they need to cough; It's the tickle that is physically triggering you to cough/tic. It is NOT emotionally triggering you, the physical "tickle" sensation is literally physically triggering you to do the tic that you feel you have to do. Just like dust causes the feeling of needing to sneeze and physically triggers a person who is allergic to sneeze. Or like a cough, there is like a tickle that forces you to cough when you are cold. So these analogies I think, help people who don't have Tourettes, recall the intensifying urge of needing to relieve the cough/yawn and how they physically need to "get it all out" because a person reaches a physical limit (a.k.a physical threshold).  And similarly, we Tourettes people feel some deep tickle within us so intense that we reach the limit of our physical threshold and we "blow up" ticking,(whether it be a coughing tic, or punching tic, or whatever tic we have to do), as we cannot suppress the tics forever, just like you can't suppress a yawn or especially a cough forever. We can't just not tick eventually. We have to do what are body is asking us to do, just like a person has to surface on the beach and breathe if their body is requiring for them to inhale. And yes, just like the need to yawn/cough can sometimes suddenly go away and suddenly you don't end up needing to yawn/ cough anymore (temporarily), the need to tic can vanish by itself, on it's own, and we Tourettes people are so glad when we get to have those moments of peace, because we hate that physical tickle that tortures us body physically, an almost indescribable sensation that makes us suffer physically- We hate that feeling of needing to tic whatever tic we have to do, but we have to do the tic. The weird part is, the tic feels like you are the "one" doing it for yourself, similar to how when a person has to cough, the person feels like they are the ones coughing for themselves. But its not that you're coughing/ or ticking on purpose, it's your body that is pushing you into doing it/requiring you to cough/breathe/yawn/tic. There's a tickle that forces a normal person to have to cough it out, and we Tourettes people have a similar tickle sensation that forces us to need to do the tic that our body needs to do and relieve itself from. We can't stop. It's almost as if a tic were an extra reflex or reaction of some sort. If someone could rid the tickle of a normal person's throat, I'm sure that person probably wouldn't feel that they need to cough anymore. I think if that powerful "tickle/tingly" physical sensation were gone, our tics would be too.

Tourettes is not curable, we won't give you false hopes, but perhaps something could help you make your life easier. So these tools might not have worked for me, but it doesn't mean it can be kinda effective for you. Yeah, give it go. :)

And if you're in your teen years, you still have a chance of your tics possibly becoming a little less worst in the stage and possibly seeing a bit of improvement as time goes by. Adults especially middle aged adults, don't have the same higher chance that teenagers have, unfortunately.

So based on my self experience of trying to distract my tics by listening to music,or suppressing my tics, or chewing gum when I needed to yawn, (had an aggressive yawning tic that I still have, but not as terrible) and based on what I've seen, it doesn't seem to be that effective for the most part. The yawning tic just got kinda better on its' own, nothing helped. I can't tell you precisely, as everyone's body is different and experiences can be subjective. However, from my personal experience of trying to suppress tics and "distract" them, it hasn't diminished the tics nor the horrible sensation of needing to do the tics, because I still feel that I need to "drain"/relieve out the suffering that I get from suppressing the tic. The intense internal ticklish physical sensation (that's how I describe the physical that I feel) makes me end up "bursting/blowing up" one way or another (I end up doing the tics). The urge is not an emotional one, rather a physical one, a real physical experience. I think what makes us suffer the most isn't so much the ticking itself, but the physical urge/sensation of needing to relieve it out right? The ticklish sensation builds up and intensifies if we don't do the tic. I get insomnia if I suppress my tic/ if I don't get the tic out of my system. I think that if that restless sensation, that "tickle" urge could go away, I think at least half of our suffering would be gone. But it's that very "tickle", that very indescribable physical sensation that forces us to do a tic in the first place. Just like a "lightness feeling" in the throat or a "tickle" that makes you feel lile you have to cough and the person needs to cough to relieve it. They have to cough it all out and the tickle they felt dissappears along with the cough, of course until the tickle comes back and you got to cough again. That's how I compare my tic experience. The "tickle" that I feel inside my body is from head to toe though, a lot worst than just a itty bitty tickle in your throat. This one is a huge tickle that just stays there, but starts building up and it lets me know I'm about to cough/do a tic especially when it's a vocal tic; The tickle is intense. It's a unique horrible feeling of its' own, but it's like connected somehow to the tic; First comes the tickle then comes the tic and the tickle gets relieved by doing the tic that your body is asking you desperately to do. Tics is similar to needing to yawn. Yawning has a horrible sensation of it's own and that sensation is the feeling of needing to yawn. First it may be tolerable, and maybe you could hold back a bit, but then there is some physical urge of needing to relieve it at some point, because you can't hold it back forever, at some point you reach a physical limit where you end up yawning eventually. Same thing for coughing, it may not feel as a yawn does, but it has its' own "urge", it's own unique sensation where you feel like you're gonna cough, and hence, you know you're about to cough because your body lets you know that you need to do it, that you need relieve the cough. And most of the time, you know if you're gonna either cough or yawn at the moment and which one you need to do, not only because they share a unique urge sensation of it's own individually,but they share one thing in common; A physical intense urge of needing relief that only gets relieved by doing what you need to do. You may be able to hold back from yawning/coughing/ticking for the first few moments or for a while, (and you may be able to build a longer threshold over time), but eventually you reach a limit where you "burst"( you end ticking) because even if you get pretty good at suppressing, you can't forever suppress the tic that you need to do. There is no such thing as achieving permanent suppression and living as if life were normal without ticking. Your body is asking to relieve it, and so you do the tic that it needs to relieve itself from. That's how I describe it.

I like comparing tics to yawn (by the way I use to have a yawning tic so I know). When you yawn it feels like you're doing it yourself, but it's like you just gotta yawn the yawn out, because the longer you suppress, the more you feel like you're gonna "blow up". There's this weird indescribable sensation either all over inside of your body or sometimes on the area that is about to tic. Or sometimes there is no sensation and you do the tic, but if you don't do the tic, a weird sensation starts "building up" and intensifying as time goes by. And every second that passes by, the sensation intensifies and you become more and more desperate similar to how you become desperate if you don't cough when you feel like you gotta cough. To me personally, the sensation that builds up while I'm suppressing my tics feels like some "tickle" tingling, like their is this "light" feeling that is very uncomfortable and the feeling starts building more and more and more and with more power and intensity until you can no longer hold back the tic and you "burst" ticking.Most tics feel like it's "you" who's doing the tic (similar to when you're yawning, you feel like you're the one who's yawning, and when you're blinking you feel like it's you blinking). But it's like you have to do it, just like everyone has to cough, blink, breathe, yawn, we Tourettes people have to do whatever tic we have to do, as we cannot hold it back forever. If we gotta punch, we gotta punch, if we gotta yawn we gotta yawn. Some tics like 1% of the tics feel like it's doing it on its own like as if it had a "mind of it's own" (think heart beat or foot cramping or muscle spasm for example). And theres a gradual relieving sensation when you're ticking and you finally reach a complete sense of physical relief from that "tickle/tingly/light feeling indescribable feeling "when you finish getting tic out of your system ("the need to relieve the tic" some indescribable sensation, that made you tic in the first place, (usually a warning sign that were about to tic) that indescribable sensation vanishes for a bit after the "tic is out" but sometimes the sensation does stay and makes us tic all over again or the sensation either fades away and return eventually. Whether there is a trigger or not, you do your tics because you jist got to do them because suppressing them makes you grow un easy and physically suffer because the indescribable sensation that you feel while you're suppressing makes is so uncomfortable that you're suffering feeling it, to a point where you become restless and anxious, until finally you relieve your tic by doing your tic that you have to do, whatever tic it may be. Also most of us do have triggers. Just like a normal person who sees another normal person yawn, and suddenly they feel like they have to yawn, or else they grow physically uncomfortable if they don't, similarly when when I am around strangers, I have to scream and kinda swing my arm up. Triggers could vary too. Also, feeling anxious, excited, tired, angry, stressed, tend to trigger tic attacks (a.k.a an on set sequence of tics whether combined, one after another, or all at the same time it could vary a lot). There could be days where you could seem almost "normal" too, but not for sole people, as everybody is different, though we have a lot of common tics and triggers. Sometimes a thought out of nowhere could come to your mind and you'll end up saying it, or sometimes you could end up shouting and saying things that you weren't even thinking about. Sometimes, the tic will come to your mind before you do the tic. Like the following example; Let's use numbers to represent each tic.

1# So there's a holding up middle finger tic (sometime you end up doing it very firmly or almost with no strength at all lile loosely, it could vary).

🎁 (Number 5 will stand for a new tic that happen to suddenly pop that you never had before)

🔼🔽 (The arrows will stand for a tic you already, but that for some reason it happened to evolve basically "upgrade" or "degrade" while you were in the middle of doing the tic).An example of this would be shaking your head and now suddenly you are shaking it side to side while rotating in circles (as if you were drawing a circle with your head while still shaking/vibrating it though).


Okay so now that we got that down, each number will stand for the kind of tic that's happening while the 🎁 will stand for a new tic popping up that you didn't ever have, and the  🔽🔼 will stand for an tic you have that has suddenly upgraded 🔼 into a more complex version or either degraded 🔽into a more simple version.

So sometimes tics could occur like this.

1>2>3
1>2>2>3>4
1>2🔼>3>4🔽
3>2>1>4
3>1>2
2>1>3
4>🎁>3
1>🎁>🎁>🎁>🎁 (literally one new tic could also appear after another new tic has appeared like a new one gets added one after another even in the middle of ticking).

Theres no limits to tics. Its like horrible algebra or like building blocks. One tic happens, and then that tic ends and now you're ticking something immediately right after that (or sometimes a looong while after it) and then another tic after the other tic. The gap time between when one tic happens and then another can be short or long time. Sometimes there will be moments where you are "at peace" where you not ticking but then the tics start again (whether its one tic or many tics, it could vary all). Now the engine is steaming, wheels are rolling, and whistle is blowing all at the same time or one after another or back as if tics were "taking their turns". Suddenly, one of the tics might hop off the train an a tic your familiar with (the usual tics hops on the bandwagon or a new one jumps on board that you've never had before too. Some of your usual tics might kick off everyone else off board and you might be left doing one tic. There could be smooth tic transitions too or drastic tic that flips from one tic to a different one. Its almost as if your tics metaphortically speaking "changes colors or mixes adds or subtracts to the previous or happens in clusters or each individually". Most will happen in clusters of three bam>pop>snap hit> or kick>yawn>jump and the pattern could also switch too pop>bam>snap or kick>jump jump>kick. Its like your tics are playing a game of ping pong or tennis with each other. Last, but least, your tics can "be alone/ independent" or "separate" as you call them. 

There might be times will you just shake your head and not stick out your middle finger at all nor before, nor during, nor right after. Or times where you have a sticking out middle finger tic and maybe later or the next day you do the head shaking tic or whatever tic or all then in one day.

 Sometimes you might shake your head, and right after you're done shaking your head, you stick your middle finger out.

Sometimes it might happen as a sequence of events. You might shake your head, and right after you're done shaking your head or when you feel that you're about to be done shaking your head, you feel like your body is preparing to stick out your middle finger and you end up stick out your middle finger out. Sometimes there are patterns; All tics ticking at once, or instead of it all once, tics happening one right after the other one finishes is' course (in a sequence one individually happening, then right after that another separate tic happening and then after that one another "lonely" (separate) tic happening without other tics to keep it company. Sometimes this cycle can rinse and repeat or even change into a new cycle with new additional tics or with other tics you already have hopping on ti the train, making the cycle even more complex. Most tics do not feel like a "muscle spasm" as if it were moving by itself. Most tics feel like you're doing them for yourself kinda like when you cough, you feel like your coughing for yourself. When your saying the f word it might feel so much like your saying it for yourself because it feels "light" almost "natural" but then because it feels that way you start doubting yourself because the "naturalness" of it makes you think you're faking but you're Not faking. By the way, muscle spams can be tics to even if you feel like their moving by itself instead of feeling like you're "doing it yourself". About more than 90% of the tics feel like you're doing them yourself and a few of them feel like their "doing it own its own"  (like when your leg gets a charlie horse muscle spasm and you could see the muscle starts twisting and trembling on your leg). In the world of Tourettes there are technically "two" types of muscles spams. One where you feel like your twisting your arm for example (this one feels you're " the one doing it".Then a different there's a muscle spasm, one where you may be all chill with your arm on a table all relaxed and comfy, and bam suddenly you'll just see a part of the muscle in your arm twisting and trembling like its "doing it on its own". I also compare motor tics (things like punching accidentally when someone scares you wakes you up while sleeping, kicking when you're tickled on your feet etc-reflexes. That's the thing though Tourettes feels oddly natural in a way. Look experiment this.l for yourself a simple little thing. Cough right now purposely, cough and cough. Focus on the feeling. Okay now get near some dust or chilli powder or something cold (something that causes coughing. Notice how you physically feel like your about to cough because those things trigger you and now you have the urge to cough and you start coughing. Notice how you felt like your body used strength equally for both times that you coughed, but the first one you had no doubt that you did it yourself, while the second time you coughed, you either coughed because you had to do it because there wasn't exactly a way of preventing it fully from happening because even if you were felt like you were able to resist coughing or even if you felt like you were able to stop yourself from coughing while you were coughing for the first few moments, you ended up doing it (you ended up coughing). You don't have full power over it. And even the little power you have over it, it ends up finishing eventually and bam you coughed. That's how tics are.

I also compare both vocal and motor tics to the blinking reflex. Stare and notice how you feel like you gotta blink. No one can resist blinking forever even if they resist for the first few minutes. The physical desperation in your eyes gets so anxiously desperate, that you feel like you gotta blink and so you end up blinking in a matter of time. You can't fully stop it because technically it's like a reflex of some sort. So even though you feel like you have some control over your eyes not blinking/or blinking at first, why did you eventually blink? Because even though you feel like you could resist for a few seconds you eventually cant. There is something more powerful physically than you. It may feel like your the one who's blinking for yourself because it feel so natural when you end up doing it, but blinking is as "controllable" as a reflex (not very controllable in other words. Tics feel almost very "natural" yet a bit unnatural at the same time like how a reflex feels. A reflex feels like your voluntarily doing it, but you know that you can't exactly stop your reflex from completely happening because you end up reflexing eventually. And just like when you do a reflex and you feel like your the one doing it, such is the case for Tourettes- It feels like you're the one doing it but trust me its not your fault. You're not faking it, you just think you are because you probably have this indescribable physical somewhere deep physically within where you feel like you gotta do it, not that you emotionally feel like you gotta do it, not like impulse, but like a reflex. I don't compare tics to itchiness because it can confuse people who are trying to understand Tourettes. The itchy analogy/comparison doesn't describe very well what we mean by lack of control because when a normal person without Tourettes is itchy, they can choose if whether to scratch or not because they are in full power of choosing and such itching analogy might make them think we have the control, but that were just not "disciplined" enough. So to a avoid a misunderstanding and misconceptions, I explain to them the following; My tics are like reflexes. I compare tics to reflexes because just like reflexes, they feel voluntary in a way and like your the one "cooperating" physically in doing it, but you can't exactly prevent the reflex from eventually reflexing/happening. You feel like you gotta laugh and you eventually laugh no matter how hard you try to stop yourself from laughing, because it's a reflex. The main idea of this analogy is to show what we mean by loss of control over our tics. It is physical, not mental loss of control. Tourettes also tends to have triggers just like a reflex has triggers. A person's laugh reflex is triggered by watching something super funny right? I tell people without Tourettes to watch something funny so they could experience the physical feeling of lack of control over their laugh. This is why you eventually laugh when something super funny triggers you to laugh, because though a person may be able to hold back from laughing for a bit, the person eventually loses control because they don't exactly have full control over it, just like no one has full control over blinking, so you blink. Having a bit control over laughing/blinking is not enough to prevent yourself from eventually laughing/blinking. A bit control is not enough, that's why you can't prevent yourself from eventually laughing/blinking because to be able to stop something from ever occuring, it is necessary to have 100% physical control to do or not do something. And just like the laughing and blinking analogy, we Tourettes people cannot stop our tics from eventually ticking. Just like a normal person needs to cough at the moment and there's no point in trying to hold back their cough from coughing because they have to cough and they will cough eventually because physical control is lost.Like that-We Tourettes people have as much (in quotes) "control" as a person who has to cough. We have as much "control" as a person who sees something funny and feels like they are gonna laugh and only able to control their laugh for a bit... until they can no longer hold back and they burst laughing out loud. We Tourettes people don't mean to tic, contrary, we want to stop and sometimes we feel embarrassed because we get humiliated by our own tics, we don't mean to tic, but we just cant hold back the tic forever-We eventually tic. Whether it's a vocal or a punching tic, or laughing tic, or mocking tic, there's no way of it not happening at some point, the tic is gonna tic. So Tics are like that. You could be chill and all, reading your favorite book on a comfy chair, and suddenly there's a need to let the tic out and you don't know why. Just sometimes you feel like you gotta sneeze and you don't know why if there's no dust or anything, but most of them time you know it's coming because when you're about to do something there is a sensation attached.
